plan.concept: The human contrast sensitivity threshold curve as a function of log(frequency), comparing a standard sensitivity profile with a degraded high-frequency sensitivity profile
plan.layout: single panel with labeled axes and two overlapping curves representing contrast sensitivity

annotations: Y-axis title 'My contrast sensitivity threshold' is positioned at the top-left, aligned horizontally above the y-axis arrow
X-axis title 'log(frequency)' is positioned at the bottom-right below the x-axis arrow
Axes cross slightly at (-0.3, -0.3) to form a standard coordinate intersection with overshooting lines

plan.colorScheme: White background, solid black axes with clean arrowheads, red curve (#FF0000) for standard sensitivity, blue curve (#0000FF) for degraded sensitivity
plan.reconstructionNotes: The axes must have arrowheads. The y-axis label should be positioned at the top left in a horizontal layout, and the x-axis label should be at the bottom right. The red and blue lines overlap exactly from x=0 to roughly x=4.3, after which the blue line drops off much more sharply than the red line.
